paragraphs.title: The Shunammite Woman Recovers Her Property

easy.explanation: Elisha said that the famine would last seven years.
easy.q: How long was the famine that Elisha warned about?

easy.explanation: She sojourned in the land of the Philistines for seven years.
easy.q: To what land did the woman go with her household?

easy.explanation: She went to the king to ask for her house and land.
easy.q: To whom did the woman cry after she returned?

medium.explanation: Elisha warned her that the LORD had called for a seven-year famine.
medium.q: Why did the woman leave the land?

answers: Her house, her land, and the fruits of the field
Only the fruits of the field
medium.explanation: The king commanded that all that was hers and the fruits of the field be restored.
medium.q: What did the king command to be restored to the woman?

medium.explanation: The woman was told to live temporarily wherever she could.
medium.q: What does “sojourn” mean in the passage?

answers: Gehazi told the king about the woman, and the king helped her
The king sent Elisha to search for her
The woman asked Gehazi to become king
challenge.explanation: Gehazi identified the woman while telling the king about Elisha’s works, and the king ordered her property restored.
challenge.q: How were Elisha’s ministry and the king’s decision connected?

answers: She wanted to receive a prophecy
She wanted her house and land returned
She wanted to leave for Philistia again
challenge.explanation: The text says that she cried unto the king for her house and land.
challenge.q: Why did the woman have reason to appeal to the king?

answers: The woman returned first, and then the king ordered her property restored
The property was restored before the woman left the land
Gehazi restored the property before Elisha warned of famine
challenge.explanation: After seven years the woman returned, appealed to the king, and then received the order of restoration.
challenge.q: What does the sequence of events show?

paragraphs.title: Hazael Rises to the Throne of Aram

easy.explanation: Ben-hadad the king of Syria was sick.
easy.q: Who was sick when Elisha came to Damascus?

easy.explanation: Ben-hadad sent Hazael to the man of God.
easy.q: Who was sent to ask Elisha about Ben-hadad’s illness?
Who reigned in Syria after Ben-hadad died?

answers: Whether he would win a war
Whether he would recover from his disease
medium.explanation: Hazael asked whether Ben-hadad would recover from his disease.
medium.q: What did Ben-hadad want to know through Hazael?

medium.explanation: Elisha settled his countenance and wept.
medium.q: How did Elisha react when he foresaw the evil Hazael would bring upon Israel?

medium.explanation: Hazael brought gifts from Damascus to Elisha.
medium.q: What is a “present” in this passage?

answers: Elisha said Ben-hadad would recover but would surely die, while Hazael reported only that he would recover
Elisha said Ben-hadad would flee, while Hazael said he would reign
Elisha gave no answer, and Hazael invented one
challenge.explanation: Elisha revealed both recovery from the disease and Ben-hadad’s certain death, but Hazael reported only the recovery.
challenge.q: What was the difference between Elisha’s answer and what Hazael told the king?

answers: He foresaw the suffering Hazael would bring upon Israel
challenge.explanation: Elisha wept because he knew the evil Hazael would do to the children of Israel.
challenge.q: What did Elisha’s weeping reveal about the future?

answers: Ben-hadad became sick, Hazael came to Elisha, Ben-hadad died, and Hazael reigned
Hazael reigned, Ben-hadad was sent to Elisha, and then he became sick
Elisha reigned, Ben-hadad died, and then Hazael brought a present
challenge.explanation: The passage records Ben-hadad’s illness, Hazael’s visit, Ben-hadad’s death, and Hazael’s accession.
challenge.q: Which sequence of events is described in the passage?

paragraphs.title: The Reign of Jehoram in Judah

easy.explanation: Jehoram was the son of Jehoshaphat.
Jehoram reigned eight years in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How long did Jehoram reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: The text says that he did evil in the sight of the LORD.
easy.q: How is Jehoram’s conduct described in the sight of the LORD?

answers: The way of the kings of Israel and the house of Ahab
The way of the kings of Syria
medium.explanation: Jehoram walked in the way of the kings of Israel, as did the house of Ahab.
medium.q: In whose way did Jehoram walk?

medium.explanation: The daughter of Ahab was Jehoram’s wife.
medium.q: What was Jehoram’s relationship to the house of Ahab?

answers: For David’s sake and because of God’s promise to him
medium.explanation: The LORD would not destroy Judah for David his servant’s sake.
medium.q: Why did the LORD not destroy Judah completely?

answers: He did evil, yet Judah was not completely destroyed
He did good, yet Judah was destroyed
He did not reign, yet he was called king
challenge.explanation: Jehoram did evil, but the LORD preserved Judah because of His promise to David.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in the account of Jehoram’s reign?

challenge.explanation: Jehoram’s marriage to Ahab’s daughter connected him to Ahab’s house.
challenge.q: Which detail explains how the house of Ahab influenced Jehoram?

answers: To preserve David’s line and kingdom for future generations
To give David a white field
To provide Judah with a new army
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to God’s promise to preserve David’s dynasty.
challenge.q: What does the phrase “to give him alway a light, and to his children” mean in context?

paragraphs.title: The Revolts of Edom and Libnah

easy.explanation: Edom revolted from under the hand of Judah.
easy.q: Who revolted from Judah in the days of Jehoram?

answers: They made a king over themselves
easy.explanation: Edom made a king over itself.
easy.q: What did the people of Edom do?

easy.explanation: Libnah revolted at the same time.
easy.q: What other place revolted against Judah?

answers: He went with all the chariots by night and smote Edom
He sent Elisha to speak with Edom
medium.explanation: Jehoram went to Zair by night and smote the Edomites and the captains of the chariots.
medium.q: How did Jehoram respond to Edom’s revolt?

medium.explanation: The people fled into their tents.
medium.q: What did the people do after the attack?

answers: Edom continued to revolt unto that day
medium.explanation: Despite Jehoram’s attack, Edom continued to revolt from Judah.
medium.q: Why can it be said that Jehoram did not gain complete control over Edom?

answers: Jehoram continued to face difficulties in his reign
Libnah was the capital of Edom
challenge.explanation: After Edom’s revolt, the text says that Libnah also revolted.
challenge.q: What does the movement from Edom’s revolt to Libnah’s revolt show?

answers: After Jehoram smote the enemy, the people fled into their tents
The people fled before Jehoram went to battle
The people fled because Elisha commanded them
challenge.explanation: The account describes Jehoram’s attack first and the people’s flight afterward.
challenge.q: What was the relationship between the battle and the people’s retreat?

answers: He died and was buried in the city of David, and Ahaziah reigned in his stead
He went to reign in Syria
Edom removed him from the throne
challenge.explanation: Jehoram slept with his fathers, and Ahaziah his son reigned in his stead.
challenge.q: How did Jehoram’s reign end according to the passage?

paragraphs.title: Ahaziah and the War with Aram

easy.explanation: Ahaziah the son of Jehoram reigned in his stead.
easy.q: Who became king of Judah after Jehoram?

easy.explanation: Ahaziah reigned one year in Jerusalem.
easy.q: How long did Ahaziah reign in Jerusalem?

easy.explanation: They went to war against Hazael king of Syria at Ramoth-gilead.
easy.q: Against whom did Joram and Ahaziah fight?

answers: The way of the house of Ahab
The way of the kings of Syria
medium.explanation: Ahaziah did evil as did the house of Ahab.
medium.q: In whose way did Ahaziah walk?

answers: He was wounded by the Syrians
medium.q: What happened to Joram in the war at Ramoth-gilead?

answers: To be healed of his wounds
medium.explanation: Joram went back to Jezreel to be healed of the wounds he received in battle.
medium.q: Why did Joram return to Jezreel?

answers: They were connected and cooperated in war
challenge.explanation: Ahaziah joined Joram in the war and later went to see him in Jezreel.
challenge.q: What does Ahaziah’s visit to Joram show about their relationship?

answers: Joram’s wounds caused him to return to Jezreel for healing
Victory over Hazael caused them to return
Libnah’s revolt caused Ahaziah to leave Judah
challenge.explanation: The text directly connects Joram’s wounds with his return to Jezreel.
challenge.q: What was the connection between the end of the battle and the return to Jezreel?

answers: His mother was Athaliah, the daughter of Omri king of Israel
challenge.explanation: Ahaziah’s mother was Athaliah, daughter of Omri, and he was the son-in-law of the house of Ahab.
challenge.q: Which family detail connected Ahaziah with the house of Ahab?
